papers.title: Surface modification of dental implants - A narrative review
papers.abstract: The dental implants have proven to be the most desired method of a replacement of the missing teeth, with the success rates of the dental implants reported to be between 90-99 per cent in the existing literature. Osseointegration, which is the close structural and functional bonding of viable bone tissue and the implant surface, is the key to the sustained performance of an implant. Surface modification has become the primary approach to improving the process of osseointegration, reducing the risk of peri-implant infections, and extending the total lifespan of implants. This narrative review will cover the history, classification, mechanism, and clinical outcomes of the surface modification methods of dental implants. Those methods covered in the review are subtractive techniques, like machining, sandblasting, and acid-etching, additive techniques, like hydroxyapatite (HA) coating and titanium plasma spraying (TPS), chemical techniques, including anodization, alkali treatment, and fluoride incorporation, and biochemical functionalization with growth factors, peptides, and drug-eluting systems. State-of-the-art technologies, such as nanoengineering, laser surface texturing, zirconia and PEEK modifications along with antimicrobial approaches are also discussed. Existing literature invariably advocates moderately rough surfaces (Ra = 102μm) as the most preferable in bone-implant contact, and the multifunctional coating of osteogenic and antibacterial properties as the future of the science of implant surfaces.

papers.title: A Neuro-Physical Framework for Three-Dimensional Elastodynamic Wave Prediction in Mechanical Components
papers.abstract: Predicting vibration-wave propagation in mechanical components requires solvingtransient, three-dimensional elastodynamic equations across complex geometries, material interfaces, and frequency-dependent damping. This paper proposes a researchframework—termed the Causal Energy-Constrained Neural Operator (CENOp)—for learning mappings from material properties, geometry, initial conditions, andexternal excitation to displacement, velocity, and stress fields.The framework combines continuum mechanics with a neural operator, enforcingmomentum balance, constitutive consistency, boundary and interface conditions, andan energy-dissipation inequality. A memory-variable constitutive model representslinear viscoelastic damping, while optional stochastic fields represent materialuncertainty. The proposed additions are hypotheses for future testing, not establishedphysical laws.A reproducible validation program is outlined using analytical wave solutions,finite-element simulations, and measurements from instrumented components. Theframework is intended as a fast surrogate for repeated forward predictions andas a tool for parameter identification, damage localization, and uncertainty-awarestructural monitoring. Its performance must be demonstrated against independentnumerical and experimental benchmarks before engineering use.

papers.title: Bayesian Hybrid Surrogate Modeling of Algorithmic Tangent Stiffness Matrices in Elastoplastic Materials
papers.abstract: The algorithmic tangent stiffness is the local derivative of the discrete constitutive stress update with respect to the strain increment. It is therefore central tothe convergence, stability, and computational cost of implicit finite-element analyses of plastic materials. This paper develops a physics-informed Bayesian hybridsurrogate framework for predicting stress and algorithmic tangent responses fromexpensive constitutive integrations. The reference constitutive structure is smallstrain associative von Mises plasticity with isotropic hardening, integrated by animplicit return-mapping algorithm. Its consistent tangent is derived by linearizingthe discrete update, rather than by differentiating a continuous-time rate equation in isolation. A Gaussian-process surrogate is then defined for the constitutive correction,with its tangent obtained as the derivative of the posterior mean. The proposedhybrid construction combines an analytical elastic or mechanistic baseline with aprobabilistic correction and imposes symmetry and thermodynamic admissibilitythrough parameterization, constraints, or explicit diagnostics. Bayesian calibration,heteroscedastic observation noise, active learning, and finite-element equilibriumcoupling are formulated in a unified notation. The work is a mathematical andcomputational framework; it does not claim a new experimental data set or reportnumerical validation results. A verification protocol is specified to assess stress error,tangent error, posterior calibration, dissipation, and global Newton convergencebefore engineering deployment.

papers.title: Plasma‐Enabled Multiscale Coupling of Gyroid Architecture and Silver Nanoparticle Biointerfaces Drives Osteogenesis in 3D‐Printed Scaffolds
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering functional bone scaffolds can be enhanced by integrating biologically instructive nanoscale surface features (e.g., nanotopography and nanoroughness), micro‐scale geometric cues (e.g., curvature and porosity), and macro‐scale mechanical properties (e.g., bulk stiffness); however, these length scales are often optimized independently. Here, we present a multiscale design framework combining additive manufacturing of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid scaffolds with plasma‐assisted nanoscale surface engineering to regulate osteogenesis. Controlled variation in strut thickness generates distinct architectural regimes with coupled changes in curvature, porosity, and compressive modulus, recapitulating key aspects of trabecular bone mechanics. Micro‐computed tomography confirms trabecular bone‐like features, while finite element modeling and compression testing reveal that thinner architectures (0.6 mm) exhibit curvature‐preserving geometry and distributed stress profiles favorable for cellular interaction. A low‐temperature plasma electroless reduction (PER) strategy enables controlled silver nanoparticle (AgNP) deposition, while polydopamine (PDA) ensures uniform, cytocompatible coatings. Notably, PDA‐AgNP‐functionalized 0.6 mm scaffolds exhibit enhanced cytoskeletal organization, mineralization, and osteogenic gene expression, accompanied by elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) and YAP/TAZ ‐associated transcriptional activity. These findings support cross‐scale coupling of architecture and nanoscale biointerfaces as a design framework for osteogenic scaffolds.

papers.title: Bayesian Synchronization of Proxy Paleorecords with Reference Chronologies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Many scientific fields compare two or more noisy time series that integrate the same process but are recorded on different time scales. In paleoclimate studies, for example, proxy measurements are collected versus stratigraphic depth in a climate archive and then converted to calendar time. Synchronizing two proxy records often requires estimating an alignment that maps the depth (or preliminary age) of an input record onto the calendar‐time scale of an absolutely‐dated target record so that corresponding proxy signals line up. Existing alignment approaches are generally optimization‐based and return a single transformation, providing limited formal uncertainty quantification. Here, we introduce BSync, a Bayesian synchronization framework that treats alignments as inference over a monotone time‐mapping function to match an input to a target record. The alignment is expressed as a transformation of the input depth (or age) scale to match the target record, achieved through a link function that locally expands and compresses the input scale. The model is parameterized through interpretable local rate parameters, enabling the specification of priors on deposition times to regularize the alignment toward physically plausible deformations. BSync jointly infers the aligned chronology and provides posterior uncertainty for the time‐warping function and the resulting age scale. In synthetic data experiments and a real‐data case study, BSync yields well‐calibrated credible intervals for the aligned time scale and achieves more accurate alignments than a state‐of‐the‐art automated method, particularly when independent age constraints are sparse.

papers.title: Enhancing student engagement in higher education: Collaborative online international learning across Nordic universities
papers.abstract: This paper examines how Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL), supported by active learning methods, enhances student engagement in higher education. The paper builds on a collaboration among three universities in the Nordic countries (Finland, Norway, and Sweden) and a joint course module focused on sustainability conducted over two years, involving a total of 510 students. The primary learning outcomes for the three courses are in the topic area of industrial marketing and purchasing, specifically analyzing firms' business networks to manage interorganizational relationships, including the firms' marketing, purchasing, and supply chain processes. The module, designed as hybrid COIL, is project-based, including synchronous and asynchronous tasks completed in small groups by applying various active learning methods. Student engagement is analyzed across five dimensions: Social, Cognitive, Behavioral, Collaborative, and Emotional. The paper develops a framework that illustrates how COIL and active learning methods enhance student engagement. The combination of tasks with group-based active learning methods is highly important, impacting students’ perceptions of engagement. Peer meetings across universities in small student groups stand out as vastly important in engaging students.

papers.title: Adaptive active learning and metaheuristic-optimized transformer framework for robust intrusion detection in software-defined networks
papers.abstract: Abstract Existing intrusion detection systems largely rely on static supervised learning models that require extensive labeled data and periodic retraining. Such approaches struggle to adapt to evolving attack patterns in dynamic software-defined networks. To address these limitations, this study proposes an adaptive intrusion detection framework that integrates uncertainty-driven active learning, metaheuristic-based feature selection, Transformer-based attack classification, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization within a unified software-defined networking architecture. Unlike conventional adaptive intrusion detection systems that rely on static feature representations or fixed learning strategies, the proposed framework continuously refines both the training data and model configuration to improve robustness against evolving cyberattacks. The proposed framework iteratively identifies informative samples for annotation, optimizes feature subsets using adaptive search, and continuously updates the classifier to maintain high detection performance under changing traffic distributions. The proposed system was evaluated using the ToN-IoT dataset and additional real-world traffic traces. Experimental evaluation on benchmark and real-world network traffic datasets demonstrated a detection accuracy of up to 97.92% and an F1-score of 97.10%. Although the optimization stage increases offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment, making it suitable for practical software-defined network environments. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. Although the optimization and active-learning stages increase offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. The results demonstrate that the complementary use of adaptive sample acquisition, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization provides an effective intrusion-detection framework for software-defined network environments.

papers.title: Assessing the Perceived Effectiveness and Identifying Challenges of In-Service Training for Staff in a Teaching Hospital: A Mixed-Method, Sequential Explanatory Study
papers.abstract: Background: In-service training of healthcare staff is one of the key components of professional development and improving the quality of services. However, previous evidence indicates that the extent of applying learned material in the workplace can be influenced by individual, organizational, and process factors. This study aimed to evaluate the perceived effectiveness of in-service training and identify its challenges and harms from the perspectives of staff and managers in a teaching hospital in Yazd. Methods: This study was conducted using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design in 2024–2025. In the quantitative phase, 309 employees were selected through stratified random sampling proportional to size and completed Esmaili’s 24-item In-Service Training Effectiveness Questionnaire. This instrument assesses employees’ perceptions of the effect of training on three dimensions: knowledge development, skill improvement, and attitude creation/change, using a 5-point Likert scale, with a total score range of 24–120. Quantitative data were analyzed using independent t-tests and one-way analysis of variance with SPSS 26. In the qualitative phase, quantitative findings were used to gain a deeper understanding of employees’ perceptions of training effectiveness and to guide the interviews. At this stage, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 purposively selected managers and employees. Qualitative data were analyzed using directed thematic analysis based on the structural, process, and contextual dimensions of the three-pronged model using MaxQDA 2020 software. Results: The mean total perceived effectiveness score was 87.57 ± 27.68 (out of 120; 73% of the maximum). The mean scores for knowledge development, skill improvement, and attitude creation/change were 21.86 ± 6.71 (out of 30), 25.79 ± 7.88 (out of 35), and 39.91 ± 13.43 (out of 55), respectively; after standardization for the number of items, the three dimensions were at a similar level (72.6 % to 73.7 % of the maximum). Scores on all three dimensions differed significantly by job group, educational level, employment status, and work experience (P < 0.001). By gender, skill improvement (P = 0.045) and attitude change (P = 0.019) differed significantly, and by age, only skill improvement did (P = 0.017). Qualitative analysis revealed the challenges of the staff training system in three main themes: structural challenges (time constraints and work pressure, poor needs assessment and educational planning, limited resources and educational infrastructure, and inadequate managerial support and motivational system); process challenges (mismatch of course content with job needs, challenges related to instructors, dominance of passive teaching methods, and poor evaluation and feedback); and contextual challenges (insufficient continuous learning culture, inadequate motivation for participation, participants' perception of limited training transfer, and reduced perceived value of training). Conclusion: The findings of this study indicate that although employees and managers have a positive attitude and relative acceptance toward in-service training, this process faces serious challenges in needs assessment, design, implementation, evaluation, and post-training support. These limitations play a key role, particularly in the application of learning in the workplace. To improve perceived effectiveness and facilitate the transfer of learning to the operational environment, revising training policies is essential. This revision should focus on accurate needs assessment based on job descriptions, designing practical content with active learning methods, empowering instructors, and especially strengthening managerial support and continuous evaluation systems.

papers.title: Addressing AIAA Aerodynamics Uncertainty Quantification Challenge with Sensitivity-Based and Diffusion Model Updating
papers.abstract: This paper presents the principles and techniques employed to address the AIAA Second Uncertainty Quantification Challenge Problem for Aerodynamics. Two distinct model updating strategies for uncertainty quantification and reduction are investigated: a sensitivity-based approach and a data-driven diffusion-model-based approach. Both methods aim to infer the posterior distributions of key aerodynamic input parameters, which are subsequently propagated through either a surrogate model or XFOIL to obtain posterior-predictive lift, drag, and moment coefficients. The diffusion model shows consistent posterior-predictive responses across both the surrogate and XFOIL, whereas the sensitivity-based approach produces sharply concentrated parameter posteriors that may represent a more limited uncertainty range. Across multiple operating configurations, the two approaches produce coherent predictive aerodynamic responses despite their differing parameter posterior structures. The findings suggest that, in uncertainty quantification challenges of this type, it is not only essential to characterize multiple sources of uncertainty but equally, if not more, critical to employ an appropriate inverse uncertainty-reduction mechanism capable of leveraging the necessarily limited observational data. Designing such inverse processes to extract maximal information from sparse data remains a central difficulty and an important direction for future research in aerodynamic uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: A Cloud Learning‐Analytics Framework for Multi‐Tier Engineering Education: A Mixed‐Methods Implementation Case Study Across Three Avionics Courses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Computer‐application‐mediated learning analytics can connect simulation, controlled measurement, and field practice, but engineering‐course evidence is fragmented across instruments and units of analysis. This article contributes (1) an adaptation‐oriented four‐stage spiral curriculum with a six‐step weekly micro‐routine and (2) an implementation‐oriented cloud learning‐analytics framework for organising evidence. The curriculum ran for one academic year across three courses as a bounded single‐site case; the framework was specified but not analytically validated. Only Radar Systems and Microwave Engineering had traceable outcome summaries. An enrolment audit identified 49 records for 45 unique students; after one withdrawal, 48 completion records represented 44 students. The quantitatively driven convergent design combined course‐level summaries with 42 archived Radar Systems text entries (43 coded segments) as embedded qualitative evidence. The institutional report documented a Radar Systems knowledge improvement of at least 20% on the pre/post test and a pass‐rate change from 63% to 81%; Microwave Engineering recorded a project mean of 82.5/100 (4/4 groups ≥ 80). Feedback concerned gamified engagement, peer learning, reduced boredom, memory reinforcement, and active learning. Kahoot! records re‐exported during revision show a same‐cohort improvement of +16.9 percentage points (Hedges g av = 1.08) for the 22 students attending both first and final quiz sessions—not an equivalent‐form pre/post gain, because sessions covered different units; an alternative pairing of 31 students yields −4.8 points (non‐significant). Otherwise, item‐level responses, paired knowledge‐test records, and rater‐level scores were not retained, so reliability coefficients, effect sizes, and confidence intervals are not reported. The results support implementation feasibility and plausible learning mechanisms, not causal efficacy.

papers.title: Multi-objective artificial pedosphere intelligence for microbial homeostasis-oriented governance of functional nanoparticle systems in complex ecosystems
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil microbial homeostasis is fundamental to sustainable agriculture and ecological resilience, yet existing machine learning approaches primarily emphasize prediction accuracy while overlooking microbial interactions, uncertainty quantification, ecological homeostasis, and decision-support for nanoparticle governance. This study proposes an Artificial Pedosphere Intelligence framework to predict the Microbial Homeostasis Deviation Score (MHDS) by integrating a Microbial Co-occurrence Graph Attention Network (MC-GAT), homeostasis-constrained learning, a Deep Kernel Gaussian Process (DKL), Bayesian Multi-Objective Optimization, and SHAP-based explainability within a unified ecological intelligence pipeline. The framework first constructs an ecological feature graph, learns biologically informed representations, estimates predictive uncertainty, and subsequently performs simulation-based optimization to identify environmentally balanced nanoparticle governance strategies. The model was implemented using Python 3.10 with PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, GPyTorch, BoTorch, and SHAP, and evaluated on the Kaggle Soil Microbe Dataset containing 100,000 soil samples. The proposed framework achieved R² = 0.962, MSE = 0.007, and MAE = 0.016, representing an approximately 2.3% improvement in R² over the strongest baseline (0.94). These findings demonstrate that biologically informed graph intelligence combined with uncertainty-aware optimization provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ecological decision support for sustainable soil management. .

papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, raising methodological and ethical questions for qualitative research instruction. This article examines how we, three experienced qualitative research instructors, integrated GAI tools into our graduate-level research methods courses. Our pedagogical approach to integrating GAI tools is situated within the broader literature on GAI in higher education and qualitative research instruction, emphasizing active learning and technological reflexivity. Our work is also guided by Ethan Mollick’s artificial intelligence (AI) principles from Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI. Using reflective narrative case examples, we demonstrate how Mollick’s principles guided ethical and methodologically responsive integration of GAI, challenged assumptions about rigor and trustworthiness, and reconfigured instructor–student relationships. We conclude by highlighting tensions between efficiency, inclusion, and epistemic responsibility and implications for qualitative research education.

papers.title: Effect of Annealing Heat Treatment on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Ti-6242 Alloy Fabricated by Laser Powder Bed Fusion Method
papers.abstract: Introduction and Objectives: Ti-6242 alloy is highly regarded in additive manufacturing due to its excellent thermal resistance. Titanium laser-based additively manufactured components, however, often require post-heat treatments because of their high solidification rate and formation of undesirable phases. The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of annealing heat treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti-6242 specimens fabricated by laser powder bed fusion method. Materials and Methods: Annealing heat treatments were conducted at three temperatures of 950, 1005, and 1050 ℃ for holding times of 1, 3, 5, and 7 hours. The resulting microstructure, phase composition, and mechanical properties were characterized using optical and scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and shear punch testing. Results: The as-built microstructure consisted of columnar primary β grains with colonies of metastable martensitic α′. Heat treatment led to decomposition of α′ and formation of more stable α and β phases. At 1005 and 1050 °C, the microstructure transformed from columnar to equiaxed, whereas at 950 °C, the columnar structure was retained. Williamson–Hall plots obtained from XRD patterns revealed a reduction in the lattice microstrain of heat treated samples compared with the as-built one. The applied heat treatment, improved both ultimate shear strength and ductility of the samples. The highest ultimate shear strength (761 MPa) and normalized displacement (0.638) were achieved at 1005 °C. Conclusion: Appropriate heat treatment leads to a more stable microstructure, reduction in lattice microstrain, and transformation of the columnar structure to an equiaxed one. This process could simultaneously enhance the ultimate shear strength and ductility compared to the as-built sample.

papers.title: Thermo‐Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Microchannel Heat Sinks: A Review of Passive Techniques and Emerging AI/ML Approaches
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of modern electronics resulted in intensified thermal management challenges, and positioned microchannel heat sinks (MCHSs) as a promising technology to dissipate high heat fluxes in next generation electronics. This review critically examines recent developments in passive thermo‐hydraulic enhancement of MCHSs, with emphasis on three major approaches: channel geometry modification, internal flow modifying structures, and working fluid enhancement. The reviewed studies are synthesized according to their underlying heat transfer mechanisms, including secondary flow generation, boundary layer redevelopment, vortex‐induced mixing, wake interaction, recirculation, and increased effective heat transfer area. Particular emphasis is placed on the balance between heat transfer enhancement and hydraulic losses, as an increase in Nusselt number alone does not necessarily indicate better thermo‐hydraulic performance. The review considers integrated and hybrid enhancement configurations, as the combined use of different flow disturbing elements provided improved heat transfer with properly designed interaction. Excessive flow blockage resulted in a pressure drop penalty and reduces the overall benefit. Nanofluids and hybrid nanofluids are also discussed, considering their potential to enhance thermal performance as well as practical concerns such as stability, increased viscosity, particle sedimentation, and higher pumping requirements. In addition, emerging AI/ML approaches are reviewed across performance prediction, deep learning, physics‐informed modelling, surrogate‐assisted optimization, reinforcement learning, and CFD–ML frameworks. The analysis indicates that AI/ML can accelerate design exploration and optimization within defined parameter domains, but limitations associated with dataset quality, extrapolation, uncertainty, and independent validation remain. Finally, key research gaps involving experimental validation, manufacturability, multi‐parameter optimization, transient thermal behavior, uncertainty quantification, and intelligent thermal control are identified. The review provides an integrated perspective for developing high performance and practically viable MCHSs for next‐generation electronics cooling.

papers.abstract: Oxide dispersion‐strengthened (ODS) alloys have been widely studied due to their excellent high‐temperature creep performance and good resistance to radiation damage. However, the conventional mechanical alloying process is associated with a prolonged preparation cycle, challenges in composition control, and limited reproducibility, posing significant obstacles to the compositional design of ODS alloys. Here, we propose a new strategy for effectively screening the composition, microstructure, and properties of Fe–14Cr–2Y 2 O 3 ‐based ODS alloys via a diffusion couple technique. A continuous Ti–Al composition gradient is established within a single diffusion couple, enabling simultaneous evaluation of multiple compositions under identical processing conditions. The inter‐diffusivity along the diffusion path is determined for alloying elements with corresponding uncertainty quantification. A Ti/(Ti + Al) ratio of 0.7 is identified as optimal, yielding a high nanoparticle number density of 7.5 × 10 22 m −3 and an average particle size of ~6 nm—performance metrics that significantly outperform those achieved at other ratios. Correspondingly, the Vickers hardness reaches a peak value of 315.8 HV at Ti/(Ti + Al) ≈0.77, attributed to the synergistic effects of dispersion strengthening and solid solution strengthening. This study establishes a rational, composition‐driven strategy for the high‐throughput design of ODS alloys tailored for nuclear applications, demonstrating that the diffusion couple technique can achieve rapid correlation and efficient screening of composition–microstructure–property relationships.

papers.title: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. We combine whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster), which reveal neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than 10 seconds in advance, with a neuromechanical digital twin to test whether optimizing intrinsic goals yields realistically embodied artificial agents that quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. Our hierarchical policy selects from a discrete library of low-level motor primitives, consistent with ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents without external reward using 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. The agents are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled on the fly experiment, comparing spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decoding future turn direction from kinematics and neural activity on the same timescales observed in flies. DIAYN, a hierarchical competency algorithm learning discrete policies that maximize behavioral entropy and the separability of induced sensory observations, achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance relative to flies. Its learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this diversity serves to maximize state-space coverage at the population level. DIAYN's latent activity also closely captures the sum-difference rule for interhemispheric encoding of kinematics in biological flies. These results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.

papers.title: Large Language Models: A Plain-Language Overview for Engineers
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are neural networks trained on huge text collections to generate text by predicting what comes next. Engineers using ChatGPT and other generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools need a clear picture of what training changes and prompts add. The article starts with the Transformer, which connects words in context, and pre-training, where models learn to predict text. It then explains how fine-tuning adapts models to requests, with reinforcement learning from human feedback using human answer rankings. Next, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies documents, while chain-of-thought prompting encourages intermediate steps and agents use tools. FlashAttention lowers training and running costs by reducing data movement during attention; quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) saves fine-tuning memory. Readers get a life cycle figure and tables comparing methods and their limits. A short checklist for judging LLM evaluation claims flags test material in training (data contamination) and model-based grading (LLM-as-a-judge). It also covers very long inputs (long context) and hallucination, meaning false or unsupported claims. Check factual accuracy separately from whether an answer sounds helpful.

papers.title: A Product-Grassmann Tucker Surrogate for Parametric Field Prediction
papers.abstract: Many-query applications such as design optimization, uncertainty quantification and digital twins call for repeated full-field predictions from expensive partial differential equation (PDE) simulations. Grassmannian reduced-order models interpolate parameter-dependent subspaces but commonly vectorize the spatial field, and the ambient dimension then grows with the product of the grid sizes. Tensor-based models preserve the multiway structure but often use shared mode-wise bases or a fixed core across parameters. We propose a Tucker-based surrogate that keeps the spatial directions and time as separate modes. The factor subspaces are interpolated on a product Grassmann manifold, Procrustes alignment places the Tucker cores in one coordinate system, and a truncated singular value decomposition models their variation. Across five PDE benchmarks in two and three spatial dimensions, including public computational fluid dynamics data, the interpolation size is reduced by factors of 13 to 482 and the stored model by factors of 13 to 464 relative to a single-subspace Grassmannian surrogate with the same local interpolation. Cached queries run 3.3 to 8.5 times faster, the mean errors over ten resampled splits differ by at most 0.22 percentage points (0.36 when every model choice is re-selected inside each split), and the prediction-error terms of the two methods differ by less than 0.1 percentage points. The remaining accuracy differences are consistent with the larger representation error of the Tucker format. In a three-dimensional grid study the interpolation-size ratio rises to 2,260 and the query speedup to 11.9 at 64^3.

papers.title: How Much Information Can We Fit inside a Transformer?
papers.abstract: How efficiently can transformers store factual knowledge? The answer to this question has implications for both model design and understanding the limits of transformer-based systems. Prior studies observe a linear relationship between the number of facts memorized and the number of model parameters required, substantially worse than what theoretical analyses predict is achievable. We re-examine empirical scaling: through rigorous and systematic experiments, including extensive hyperparameter search via Bayesian optimization, we determine the smallest model that can perfectly memorize a given set of facts, and measure how this minimum size scales with the number of facts. On synthetic datasets of random, independent (subject, relation, object) triples---e.g., (Paris, capital_of, France) ---drawn at random with no exploitable structure, we find that memorization capacity, the size of the largest dataset that a model memorizes completely, grows exponentially with the transformer dimension. Equivalently, the minimum transformer dimension $d_{\min}$ required to memorize $N$ facts grows logarithmically in $N$. Across 11 dataset sizes spanning $N = 45$ to $49{,}920$, a lack-of-fit F-test does not reject the logarithmic fit (with an offset), but it does reject all other tested alternatives including power-law. Along the depth axis, however, at fixed width, the maximum memorizable dataset size grows sublinearly with the number of layers over the measured range. We further extend our exploration to structured data containing symmetric relations or two-hop composition. In this setting, we find that transformers exploit these regularities to further improve capacity. All code to reproduce our results is available at https://github.com/Magronox/transformer_information_capacity.

papers.title: Reliability Assessment of FRP-RC Columns Using AK-MCS with a Piecewise Two-Branch Approach
papers.abstract: Slender concrete columns reinforced with fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) bars fail at medium to high axial load levels either by concrete crushing or by loss of stability, while the tensile strains in the reinforcement remain far below the rupture strain. Each non-linear finite element (FE) analysis yields only the capacity of the governing failure mode, and the governing mode changes over a broad zone in which both capacities are nearly equal. Both characteristics conflict with active-learning Kriging-assisted Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), which assumes a single, smooth limit-state function. This paper proposes a piecewise, two-branch AK-MCS framework in which each failure mode is represented by its own Kriging model, trained only on the FE analyses in which that mode governs, and the governing prediction is the minimum of both. Safeguards against data starvation keep rarely governing branches usable. After convergence, additional FE analyses are placed based on a leave-one-out calibration check and on the width of the confidence interval on the reliability index. A design-point search on the surrogate and importance sampling at the design points provide the reliability index even where direct Monte Carlo simulation finds no failure. For an FRP-reinforced concrete column example with mixed failure, 79% and 62% of the training points lie near the mode boundary. The reliability index from the design-point search agrees with the Monte Carlo estimate to within 0.05, and an FE analysis at the design point confirms the surrogate to within 0.6%.

papers.title: From Explaining to Enabling: Actionable Transparency in Algorithmic Insurance Pricing
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) systems increasingly make consequential decisions about individuals, including credit, hiring, and insurance. Research on ML-driven insurance pricing has asked how the pricing mechanism itself can be made accountable. Yet it remains unclear how an individual policyholder's algorithmically determined premium should be explained to them. We argue that a useful explanation must be valid, actionable, and reliable. A valid recommendation lowers the premium according to the model. An actionable recommendation changes only characteristics the policyholder can control. A reliable recommendation has an actual outcome that is likely to meet the target, even in sparsely observed regions of the feature space where the model is uncertain. We formalize these three requirements as axioms and develop a method that turns an algorithmic premium into recommendations that meet them. The method meets the third requirement with a Conformal Prediction constraint, which screens out recommendations that the model is too uncertain about and thereby bounds the rate of unreliable recommendations. We apply four Counterfactual Explanation techniques to 57,832 real Florida flood-insurance claims and 98,058 synthetic driver-telematics policies. We adapt these techniques for insurance applications, so that their recommendations change only controllable characteristics and resemble policyholders observed in the data. In our illustrations, the constrained recommendations for high-risk policyholders are both more reliable and associated with larger predicted risk reductions than the unconstrained ones. These results suggest that insurers can give policyholders explanations that are both actionable and trustworthy. The work contributes to research on algorithmic accountability and offers implications for insurers and regulators.

papers.title: From Human Intent to In-Orbit Action: A Self-Learning Large Language Model Agent for 6G Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Autonomous control of sixth-generation (6G) low Earth orbit satellite networks is hindered by the gap between high-level human intent and low-level control logic: translating a request such as "uninterrupted Arctic video" into a valid reinforcement learning reward still takes days of manual trial and error, and existing large language model translators cannot learn from the failures of the policies they generate. This article presents ALMOND (Agentic Large-Model-Orchestrated autonomous Network Design), a cognitive framework that closes this intent-to-action loop under on-orbit compute constraints. The contribution in artificial intelligence is a bidirectional semantic engine that translates natural-language demands into multi-objective reward functions and, conversely, mines implicit operational constraints from failed reinforcement-learning trajectories through counterfactually validated forensics, together with a large language model-guided graph neuroevolution that seeds and critiques policy architectures. The contribution in engineering is a ground-centric, compute-frugal architecture for autonomous 6G non-terrestrial network operation, in which satellites execute only distilled policies below 50,000 parameters with sub-15 ms inference and no on-board large language model. On a 350-satellite digital twin driven by real ephemeris data, ALMOND raises polar handover success from 55% to over 95%, converges about three times faster than baseline reinforcement learning, and reduces reward engineering from 48 hours to 4.5 hours, demonstrating a practical path toward trustworthy in-orbit autonomy.

papers.title: SHIFT-JEV: Certified Abstention and Gain-Gated Continual Adaptation for LLM-Based Decision Models under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can act as decision models that return a probability distribution over a fixed set of options, but deployed decision models face domain, label-prior, emerging-class and candidate-set shift. We study how such models fail under shift and propose SHIFT-Jev, a monitoring, abstention and continual-adaptation procedure for them. It scores the risk of each decision from uncertainty, format and option-consistency signals, certifies abstention thresholds with Learn-then-Test, monitors the decision stream with drift and label-shift detectors, and accepts a model update only when an expected-gain gate finds a significant held-out improvement without loss on earlier regimes. On a benchmark of ten shifted test environments with Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-4B (three seeds each) and Phi-4-mini, fine-tuning with KL anchors and temperature scaling lowers calibration error under shift from 0.289 to 0.087. At a target risk of 10%, a learned uncertainty score with a certified threshold exceeds the target in 3 to 5 of 27 environment-seed tests, against 5 to 15 for a max-probability score with the same certification and 9 to 14 for conformal prediction sets; drift-based routing changes little. A chi-squared test on predicted labels detects 95 to 99% of class-prior shifts that confidence- and embedding-based detectors miss. In continual adaptation, SHIFT-Jev reaches 70.5% accuracy on Qwen3-0.6B, above replay, LwF, EWC and fine-tuning baselines in every seed, whereas on Qwen3-4B its conservative gate leaves it 0.4 to 1.4 points behind them.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction with Stable Measurement Mechanisms
papers.abstract: In applications such as air-quality monitoring, inexpensive sensor readings can help predict pollutant concentrations measured by a separate reference instrument. We study how to adapt conformal prediction intervals to a new population when reference outcomes are available in the source data, but only sensor readings and context, such as weather conditions, are available in the target. We assume that the measurement distribution at a given outcome and context remains stable, while context frequencies and outcome distributions may change. This model is a particular form of causal mechanism shift. Its statistical restriction has been studied as sparse joint shift. Using established marginal matching, predictive adjustment, and weighted conformal calibration, we examine what this restriction contributes to coverage and interval length for continuous outcomes. Gaussian analyses show how measurement stability can identify outcome changes and how retaining context can shorten prediction intervals. For Gaussian models with known source mechanisms, we derive exact coverage formulas in the large-calibration limit while keeping the unlabeled target sample finite. These formulas explain when sharing a correction across contexts is preferable to fitting separate corrections, and why estimating outcome variability is particularly sensitive to weakly informative measurements. Experiments on synthetic Gaussian data show a coverage gain over covariate weighting at the same mean length and a length reduction of about $8\%$ relative to pooled label adjustment at comparable coverage. On the Air Quality dataset, controlled shifts yield coverage gains with longer intervals, while spring-to-autumn and year-over-year transfers show substantial undercoverage.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Crowd Flow Control Using Dynamic Barriers
papers.abstract: Crowd barriers are widely used to regulate pedestrian movement during large public events such as pilgrimages. However, fixed barrier layouts often create unnecessary stopping and local congestion even when they successfully control the overall crowd flow. Finding better barrier configurations is difficult because there is no dataset that provides the best barrier placement for a given crowd scene. We address this challenge by introducing a simulation-driven reinforcement learning framework that learns barrier configurations without requiring labelled training data. Starting from a segmented crowd scene, we construct a realistic simulation environment that reproduces the observed pedestrian distribution. This environment is then used to train a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent that continuously adjusts barrier positions to improve pedestrian movement. Unlike supervised approaches the proposed framework allows the agent to explore barrier configurations that have never been observed in real data. We evaluate the learned policy under unseen numbers of pedestrians. The learned policy consistently outperforms the existing manually designed barrier configuration by reducing pedestrian stops while maintaining effective flow regulation. These results demonstrate that combining computer vision crowd simulation and reinforcement learning provides an effective framework for optimizing crowd control infrastructure.

papers.abstract: One of the fundamental differences between biological neural networks and artificial neural networks (ANNs) is that biological neurons obey Dale's principle: each neuron projects either exclusively excitatory or exclusively inhibitory outputs. While this constraint is central to biological circuits, previous attempts to impose Dale's principle in ANNs have often led to training instability or degraded performance. In this work, we introduce EISep RNN, a recurrent neural network architecture that implements Dale's principle through a learnable excitatory-inhibitory separation. Across a series of learning settings, including multi-task learning, continual learning, and reinforcement learning, EISep achieves more stable training dynamics, competitive or improved performance, and sparser, more modular connectivity than vanilla RNNs and previous Dale-constrained models. EISep also exhibits stable and informative latent dynamics. These results establish Dale's principle as a biologically grounded and computationally effective inductive bias for recurrent neural networks.

papers.title: Performance of Neural Operator Baselines on 'The Well' Dataset
papers.abstract: The Well, a 15-terabyte dataset spanning 16 physical simulation domains, provides an extensive benchmark for developing and evaluating machine learning surrogate models for complex physical systems. The baselines released with the benchmark were presented by their authors as illustrative examples obtained at small computational cost, trained with zero to very limited hyperparameter tuning and under a highly constraining 12-hour per-run wall-clock limit. These results have subsequently been treated as fully tuned benchmarks, and in some cases effectively interpreted as unconstrained performance baselines. We perform a short non-exhaustive hyperparameter search for the Tucker-factorized Fourier Neural Operator (TFNO) under the same 12-hour per-run wall-clock limit, while using only a single input timestep rather than the history of up to four used by the published baselines. Despite this more restrictive setup, tuning alone reduces VRMSE below both published FNO and TFNO baselines on 15 of 17 tasks, sometimes by several orders of magnitude. This sensitivity to a modest tuning effort underscores that the released neural operator baselines should not be treated as architectural benchmarks.

papers.title: Functional Surface Self‐Assembly on Nitinol Biliary Stents for Enhanced Anti‐Fouling and Low‐Friction Behavior
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitinol (NiTi) stents are widely used for biliary decompression, but their biofluid‐exposed metallic surfaces remain susceptible to mechanical irritation, bacterial colonization, sludge deposition, and inflammation‐associated restenosis. Inspired by the dynamic, low‐adhesion interfacial function of the native glycocalyx, we developed a self‐assembled slippery liquid‐infused porous surface (SASLIPS) for NiTi biliary stents. The modified surface formed a continuous liquid‐infused architecture, exhibited water sliding angles <0.5°, and reduced adhesion under the tested conditions. SASLIPS decreased the coefficient of friction (COF) from 0.69 (NiTi) to 0.09 (SASLIPS), reduced biliary sludge accretion, inhibited 96.98% of E. coli adhesion and biofilm formation, and attenuated inflammatory responses, while preserving macroscopic thermally induced shape recovery. Molecular dynamics simulations supported favorable interactions between perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) and perfluorodecalin (PFD) and showed that the PFD‐rich interfacial region reduced water and cholesterol access to the modeled substrate. In a porcine study with independent 1‐ and 6‐month cohorts, SASLIPS‐coatedstents showed 89.92% lower sludge‐associated autofluorescence than bare NiTi stents at 1 month and no gross evidence of luminal obstruction at the 6‐month retrieval. This work established a liquid‐infused fluorinated surface strategy for engineering anti‐fouling, anti‐inflammatory, and mechanically compatible biliary stents, and offered a materials‐driven solution to persistent interfacial failure in biofluid‐rich implant environments.

papers.abstract: Aim: To evaluate morphometric characteristics relevant to immediate implant planning in the maxillary anterior region using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Materials and Methods: In this retrospective study, CBCT images of 597 maxillary anterior teeth, including central incisors, lateral incisors, and canines, from 119 individuals were analyzed. Labial bone thickness, sagittal root position, apical bone height, labial concavity, undercut depth, and alveolar width were assessed. For each tooth, two virtual implant placement strategies were simulated: prosthetically driven and bone-driven. Results: Labial bone thickness was <1 mm in most cases, and sagittal root position predominantly exhibited a Class III distribution (77.8%). Apical bone height was generally adequate for primary stability. More pronounced undercuts and concavities were observed in the lateral incisors. Prosthetically driven implant placement was associated with an increased risk of facial bone compromise, whereas the bone-driven approach resulted in safer implant positioning. Conclusion: Immediate implant planning in the maxillary anterior region frequently requires a bone-driven approach, primarily because of thin labial bone and root-position characteristics. CBCT-based three-dimensional evaluation plays a critical role in achieving safe, predictable, and individualized implant planning.

papers.title: C-MixNet: Regime-aware clustering and MDN-augmented LUBE for uncertainty-aware wind power forecasting
papers.abstract: Wind power forecasting under uncertainty remains a critical challenge due to non-stationary patterns, regime shifts, and fluctuating dynamics across time. Existing interval-based methods often struggle to generalize across heterogeneous operating conditions, resulting in inconsistent coverage and suboptimal reliability. This paper presents C-MixNet, a hybrid framework that integrates regime-aware clustering, Mixture Density Network (MDN), and Lower Upper Bound Estimation (LUBE) for robust Prediction Interval (PI) generation. Using three years of SCADA data from a Vestas V52 turbine in Ireland, we first segment the dataset into regimes using an ensemble of Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Self-Organizing Map (SOM), and K-Means Clustering Algorithm (K-Means), resolving label disagreement via majority voting and measuring agreement with Cohen’s kappa scores. For each cluster, we train dedicated MDN models to extract probabilistic forecasts and embed their outputs, including component weights, means, and variances, into the feature space, enabling LUBE to learn enriched uncertainty-aware representations. To manage the dimensionality introduced by MDN features, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) based feature selection is employed, although reduced models underperform. We then incorporate MDN-derived predictive bounds as additional features, which substantially improve LUBE performance. Conformal prediction is further explored for calibrated interval estimation but shows limited improvement under the considered evaluation criteria. Additional validation examines temporal dependency, cross-turbine applicability, and comparison with a conventional probabilistic benchmark. Ultimately, the MDN-augmented LUBE framework achieves the best trade-off in Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP), Prediction Interval Normalized Average Width (PINAW), and Coverage Width-based Criterion (CWC) across clusters. Extensive experiments with ten repeated trials validate the consistency and robustness of the proposed approach. This work contributes a modular, regime-adaptive, and interpretable framework for uncertainty-aware wind power forecasting, with strong potential for real-world deployment in energy markets and operational dispatch systems.

papers.title: Residual stress and multiscale microstructural evolution in steels processed by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing can produce metallic components with complex geometries, but residual stress induced by non-equilibrium thermal histories still limits dimensional stability, crack resistance, fatigue performance, and service reliability. Thermal gradients and constrained cooling are central to residual stress formation, but they cannot fully explain how residual stress develops in steels that undergo solid-state phase transformations. This review compares residual stress and multiscale structures in non-transforming and phase-transforming steels, with these terms used operationally for LPBF residual stress analysis. In the non-transforming regime, no major build-cycle solid-state transformation strain is required to interpret the as-built residual stress state, whereas in phase-transforming steels thermal contraction interacts with transformation strain. The comparison is organized around LPBF thermal history, stress generation mechanisms, phase transformation, and measurement conditions used to report residual stress. In this review, non-transforming steels, represented by predominantly austenitic LPBF 316L under the conditions considered here, are used as the thermal-stress-dominated reference case, in which melt pool gradients, scan history, heat accumulation, build plate constraints, and post-processing treatments control stress evolution without requiring a major contribution from martensitic transformation strain. Phase-transforming steels, such as H13 hot-work tool steel, add martensitic or bainitic transformation, retained austenite, intrinsic tempering, carbide evolution, and preheating-dependent phase evolution to this pathway. These metallurgical processes can reduce, redistribute, or locally change the sign of the measured stress. Reported residual stress values should therefore be interpreted together with measurement depth, gauge volume, stress component, build state, phase selection, and stress scale. Further progress depends on transformation-aware process design, phase-resolved three-dimensional characterization, and models that link LPBF process history to the measured residual stress state.

papers.title: Educational Interventions for Perinatal Depression Management Among Non-Specialist Providers in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Descriptive Systematic Review of Limited Evidence
papers.abstract: This descriptive systematic review synthesizes evidence from resource-constrained primary and non-specialist care settings on the structural components of educational interventions for frontline health care workers regarding perinatal depression (PND). A comprehensive search was conducted across CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Scopus for experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between January 1, 2019, and August 31, 2025, in Resource-Constrained Settings. Three quasi-experimental, non-randomized studies met the pre-specified inclusion criteria, representing a total of 351 participants across Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Thailand. Quality appraisal conducted via the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions, Version 2 (ROBINS-I V2) tool judged all 3 studies to be at an overall critical risk of bias. A descriptive narrative synthesis was conducted in accordance with the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines, as high clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded a statistical meta-analysis. Preliminary patterns across the included studies suggest that educational models in these settings commonly feature standardized reference frameworks such as the World Health Organization (WHO) Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) and structured active learning approaches. Multi-session delivery formats, cascade (train-the-trainer) models, and practical clinical phases accompanied by remote mobile supervision were reported alongside improvements in immediate provider-level metrics. The extremely narrow evidence base, high attrition rates, lack of comparative control groups, and complete absence of patient outcomes severely constrain the ability to draw definitive conclusions regarding intervention effectiveness or causal mechanisms. The findings are presented as hypothesis-generating, emphasizing the critical need for methodologically rigorous trials in global maternal mental health.

papers.title: Nonlinear Mathematical Modeling of Crop Growth and Biomass Accumulation for Accurate Yield Prediction in Smallholder Farming Systems
papers.abstract: Accurate yield prediction in smallholder farming systems remains a central challenge in agricultural science, particularly across sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Southeast Asia, where resource constraints, climate variability, and data scarcity severely limit the applicability of conventional linear models. This paper presents a comprehensive review and synthesis of nonlinear mathematical frameworks for modeling crop growth and biomass accumulation, with emphasis on their suitability for smallholder contexts. We examine logistics, Gompertz, Richards, and betafunction growth models, as well as process-based dynamic simulation approaches including APSIM, DSSAT, and AquaCrop, and evaluate their integration with remote sensing data and machine learning algorithms. Key findings indicate that hybrid models combining physiological process descriptions with data-driven optimization consistently outperform purely empirical or mechanistic approaches, particularly when calibrated with local agronomic data under variable input conditions. We further discuss parameter identifiability, model parsimony, and uncertainty quantification as critical requirements for deployment in data-limited smallholder environments. papers.abstract: Distributed-drive electric vehicles can coordinate active front steering (AFS) and direct yaw-moment control (DYC) to regulate lateral and yaw responses. This study develops a hierarchical AFS–DYC framework with a unified physical interface and four-wheel torque allocation. Linear time-varying model predictive control (LTV–MPC) and sliding mode control (SMC) are compared using the same vehicle model, trajectory, feedback signals, speed loop, and allocator. The interface converts the LTV–MPC yaw-acceleration-equivalent input into an additional yaw-moment demand, which SMC supplies directly. In a 15 s CarSim/Simulink double-lane-change co-simulation at 80 km·h−1 and μ = 0.5, the implemented LTV–MPC configuration reduced the lateral-position root-mean-square error (RMSE), heading-angle RMSE, directly recorded CarSim yaw-rate RMSE, and root-mean-square (RMS) sideslip angle by 33.83%, 52.04%, 54.185%, and 49.45%, respectively, relative to SMC. The aggregate mean-squared wheel-torque command cost was approximately 5.65% lower, while the differential-component cost was 115.09% higher. A separate steering-interface hardware-in-the-loop test supported closed-loop operation of the physical steering actuator. For this maneuver, the LTV-MPC configuration showed lower tracking errors and aggregate torque-command cost, but higher differential torque demand.

papers.title: Bioactive Glass Scaffolds for Periodontal Regeneration: From Ion-Mediated Signaling and Osteoimmunomodulation to Precision Regenerative Dentistry
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The challenges of periodontal and craniofacial defects are complicated due to the hierarchical organization of oral tissues and the limited competency of the bone–ligament–cementum interface to be used as such an experimental tool. The present paper gives a critical overview of the development of bioactive-glass-based scaffolds for precision regenerative dentistry. Methods: This narrative review evaluates bioactive-glass scaffolds for periodontal and craniofacial regeneration, integrating compositional engineering, therapeutic ion signaling, osteoimmunomodulation, scaffold architecture, translational potential, and evidence limitations. Results: Bioactive glasses act as materials capable of much more than simply offering passive osteoconductive function and behave as dynamic ion delivery platforms that control hydroxycarbonate apatite formation processes, osteogenesis, angiogenesis, immune response, and antimicrobial processes. These effects include pathways such as MAPK/ERK, Wnt/β-catenin, BMP/Smad and macrophage polarization. New approaches at development involve smart and stimuli-responsive system, growth factor delivery, stem cell interfaces and patient-specific biofabrication. Mechanical constraints, degradation control, manufacturing stability and the paucity of clinical data, however, are still important limitations to translation. Conclusions: Bioactive-glass-based scaffolds are a potentially good basis for periodontal and craniofacial regeneration. Mechanistic knowledge filled with information on therapeutic ion engineering, artificial intelligence and digital manufacturing could speed up the realization of patient-specific, multifunctional and clinically translatable regeneration solutions.

papers.title: Hierarchical multi-material PEEK absorbers with Minkowski-fractal and TPMS architectures for broadband plane-wave microwave absorption
papers.abstract: Achieving broadband microwave absorption in a compact, additively manufacturable structure requires both effective impedance matching and sufficient electromagnetic attenuation; highly lossy composites alone can compromise matching at the incident surface. A multi-material poly(ether ether ketone) (PEEK)-based Minkowski pyramid structure with graded sheet-Gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) infill was designed and fabricated by fused deposition modeling (FDM). Glass-fiber-reinforced PEEK, carbon-black-filled PEEK, and carbonyl-iron-powder-filled PEEK were spatially assigned to impedance-matching, dielectric-loss, and magnetic-loss regions, respectively, to separate the functions that are difficult to optimize in a single homogeneous material. The graded sheet-Gyroid infill regulates the through-thickness effective-impedance transition, while the six-layer Minkowski-fractal pyramid introduces a macroscopic geometry for broadband wave interaction. Simulations predicted reflection loss ( RL ) below −10 dB over 2.0–18.0 GHz and favorable simulated TM-polarized oblique-incidence performance. A 325 mm × 325 mm metal-backed prototype was evaluated by the arch method under normal incidence, exhibiting effective absorption over 4.17–18.0 GHz and an additional band from 2.17 to 3.34 GHz. The measured dominant resonance frequencies agreed well with the simulated values. This work presents a hierarchical multi-material design strategy for FDM-fabricated PEEK-based broadband microwave absorbers.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Adaptive Cost Calibration in Active Learning for Parkinson’s Disease Biosignals
papers.abstract: Confirmatory labels for Parkinson’s disease (PD), from expert examination or, prospectively, biological assays, are costly, and missed cases and false alarms carry unequal consequences. ClinRisk-LLM is a framework for label-efficient, cost-aware learning from gait and speech signals in which a large language model (LLM) translates a predefined safety specification into a frozen policy setting the positive-class weight of a support vector machine and the priority of potential missed cases for annotation. Cost-sensitive training, risk-aware querying and the LLM policy were ablated on gait (n=165) and speech (n=252) data and benchmarked against post hoc thresholding, a refer-all policy, held-out gait studies and an independent speech cohort. With half of the labels, cost-sensitive active learning reduced the 4:1 asymmetric cost by 34.1% (gait) and 5.7% (speech) relative to standard active learning, at the expense of specificity. ClinRisk-LLM translated the predefined safety specification into a frozen, auditable policy that adjusted risk settings during label acquisition. Component-wise analyses indicated that classifier weighting accounted for most of the observed cost reduction, while the incremental benefit of LLM-guided adaptation varied across datasets and comparison settings. A threshold-tuned symmetric model came within 1.3 cost points for gait, and gait remained roughly level with referring everyone. ClinRisk-LLM reached a gait cost of 47.60 versus 46.10 for fixed cost-sensitive learning; 40 policies generated across three LLMs from a reconstructed specification yielded gait costs of 52.1–75.8. Applications to molecular triage remain prospective. Code and data availability details are provided in the Data Availability Statement.

papers.abstract: This academic article aims to synthesize knowledge on coaching based on the Four Bases of Success (Iddhipada 4) as a mechanism for developing teachers’ competencies to enhance the quality of active learning management in the context of the Krabi Primary Educational Service Area Office. It examines the relationships among the concepts of active learning, teacher competency development, coaching, and the Four Bases of Success (Iddhipada 4), namely Chanda (aspiration), Viriya (perseverance), Citta (dedication), and Vimamsa (investigation). The study employed a synthesis of documents, concepts, theories, and related research, together with an analysis of the teacher development context of the Krabi Primary Educational Service Area Office, where the diversity of school contexts affects teacher competency development.The synthesis revealed that coaching is a teacher professional development process emphasizing learning through authentic practice, mentoring, reflection, and continuous improvement. When integrated with the Four Bases of Success (Iddhipada 4) it strengthens teachers’motivation, commitment, and self-development, resulting in the enhancement of competencies in instructional design, active learning management, the use of instructional media and technology, assessment and evaluation, as well as educational research and innovation. Furthermore, continuous coaching contributes to the establishment of a Professional Learning Community (PLC) and a learning-oriented organizational culture, which are important outcomes supporting the improvement of teacher quality and school quality.The synthesized knowledge indicates that integrating the Four Bases of Success (Iddhipada 4) with the coaching process can serve as a conceptual framework for formulating policies, establishing teacher development systems, and designing professional development programs that are aligned with school contexts. papers.title: Negosiasi Keberanian Berkomunikasi dalam Ruang Pembelajaran: Studi Kualitatif tentang Partisipasi Komunikatif Siswa melalui Active Learning
papers.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan memahami pengalaman siswa dalam menghadapi hambatan dan menegosiasikan keberanian berkomunikasi selama mengikuti kegiatan Active Learning di MI Ma’arif NU Ngering, Kabupaten Pasuruan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus yang melibatkan lima siswa kelas V melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik berdasarkan perspektif Communication Apprehension McCroskey. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa siswa cenderung lebih aktif dalam percakapan informal dan diskusi kelompok dibandingkan ketika berbicara secara individual di depan kelas. Kekhawatiran terhadap kesalahan dan penilaian negatif teman berkaitan dengan keraguan dalam menyampaikan pendapat. Selama empat minggu pelaksanaan program, terlihat perkembangan awal dalam kesediaan siswa untuk tampil, meskipun sebagian masih menunjukkan rasa malu dan berbicara dengan suara pelan. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya lingkungan pembelajaran yang mendukung partisipasi komunikatif siswa.

papers.title: “BIOMAS EM AÇÃO”: JOGO COMO UMA FERRAMENTA PARA A INTERFACE ENTRE CIÊNCIA, INOVAÇÃO E SOCIEDADE
papers.abstract: Introduction: The notorious political complexity that enables anthropic actions, which often interfere with food chains, causing imbalance and degradation of ecosystems, can be considered an important justification for deepening theoretical knowledge related to different biomes. Several studies demonstrate that games lead individuals to deal with conflicts and develop strategies for victory, being used as tools to convey specific didactic content. Objective: The present manuscript proposes as a technical product the card game “Biomes in Action”. This game will provide resources that stimulate students to question and investigate environmental problems resulting from anthropic action. Method: The game proposes a competition among different trophic levels and can be played with one or four biomes. It allows the division of classes into groups organized with no more than four players. The objective of the game is to build the most complete food chain possible within a given biome. Results: The game will function as an active learning activity, enabling students to construct the concept of food chains in a concrete, visual, and collaborative way, in a pedagogical approach that places the student at the center of learning. Conclusion: The use of the game will allow educator intervention during the process, awakening in the class an investigative and critical attitude, considering that maintaining the balance of ecosystems is the basis for promoting environmental health. It will also contribute to raising awareness about the interdependence between healthy ecosystems and human well-being.
